headline: Volodymyr Zelensky announces a record prisoner swap after meeting America's envoys
standfirst: Fresh from the Kremlin, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Volodymyr Zelensky near Dublin, who announced the war's largest prisoner exchange and a seat for Europe at the table. Donald Trump says he no longer needs a deal with Iran, Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia's boss, Spain holds its first general strike since 2012, and Amnesty accuses the UN of failing to act before a massacre in South Sudan.

essentials.title: In Dublin, Volodymyr Zelensky announces a record prisoner swap and Europe's seat at the table
essentials.standfirst: Ukraine's president says Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, whom he received on Thursday evening on their way back from the Kremlin, promised him the biggest prisoner exchange of the war. Europeans are expected to join the next round of talks, though Moscow has not confirmed it.
body: On the evening of Thursday 12 November, at Baldonnel air base west of Dublin, Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, received America's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, a few hours after their meeting with Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin, the Kyiv Independent reports.

Mr Zelensky says the meeting “unblocked” the three-way talks, paved the way for the largest exchange of prisoners of war since 2022 and secured direct European representation at the next session, with Mr Kushner arguing that no deal is possible without Europe, according to the Kyiv Post.

No date has yet been set for the new round, whose format the Kremlin has not confirmed, while the “coalition of the willing” is due to meet in Berlin next week and EU leaders will weigh Kyiv's financing needs for 2027 on 26-27 November.

figure.compare: final figure and timetable not yet announced, according to the Kyiv Post

positions.wants: Europe directly represented on the negotiating team from the next meeting, and an agenda devoted to de-escalation and ceasefires.
A deal struck with the Europeans at the table, according to Jared Kushner; Steve Witkoff says a new meeting is already scheduled.
Has not officially confirmed that the Europeans will take part in the next round of talks.

items.name: Baldonnel air base
items.note: Casement Aerodrome, west of Dublin, where Volodymyr Zelensky received the American envoys on Thursday evening.

analysis.title: Europe still searching for its voice
analysis.text: The European Political Community summit, which brought more than 50 leaders to Dublin, mostly showed how hard Europeans find it to agree on who should speak for them to the Kremlin, notes EU Perspectives. Estonia's prime minister, Kristen Michal, proposed the president of the European Council, António Costa, and the EU's foreign-policy chief, Kaja Kallas; Emmanuel Macron replied that “content determines format”. A declaration backed by France and signed by 39 countries states that any question touching on European security must be settled with the Europeans, according to the Kyiv Post. The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, and Mr Costa promised to keep up “substantial” financial and military support for Ukraine.

keys.title: The humanitarian track
keys.text: In Abu Dhabi, negotiators had discussed swapping 1,000 to 1,500 prisoners on each side, without settling on a figure or a timetable. Jared Kushner says the agreement on the exchange has now been finalised, according to the Kyiv Post.

keys.title: Europe's winter aid
keys.text: The EU announced 500 generators from its emergency reserves, 200 buses and four floating bridges supplied by Norway. The Commission is due to present a 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, according to Interfax-Ukraine.

essentials.title: Donald Trump says he no longer needs a deal with Iran and sidelines JD Vance
essentials.standfirst: America's president said on Thursday that the time for a deal with Tehran had passed and told his vice-president to turn to other matters. In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran says two tankers caught fire after hitting mines.
body: On Thursday 12 November Donald Trump wrote that America did “not need a deal with Iran” and told his vice-president, JD Vance, who had been considering a meeting with the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, to focus on crime in Democratic-run cities, Middle East Eye reports.

The reversal, days after he spoke of “momentum” towards a settlement, comes as Tehran denies any planned meeting in Qatar, refuses to send its enriched uranium abroad and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed until its conditions are met.

Iran's navy says two tankers caught fire on Thursday after hitting mines, a claim that could not be verified, and Brent crude climbed back above $94 after the president's message, according to HNGN, while Israel is said to be preparing to strike Iran, according to the public broadcaster Kan.

figure.label: tankers ablaze on Thursday after hitting mines, according to Iran's navy
figure.compare: after three reported on Tuesday and three on Sunday

positions.wants: No deal needed any more, according to Donald Trump; the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, believes America holds the upper hand in Hormuz and is in no hurry.
Officially denies that any talks had been scheduled in Qatar.
Was due to host a meeting between JD Vance and Mohsen Rezaei, according to Turkey's intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin.

analysis.title: Diplomacy without a spokesman
analysis.text: An administration official declined to say whether the talks had been halted, and the White House has not said who will now speak to Tehran on Washington's behalf, HNGN reports. Iran makes reopening Hormuz, which it says could be done in two days, conditional on the lifting of sanctions and of America's blockade of its ports, and on an end to fighting on every front; the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, calls those demands “unacceptable”, according to CBS News. Commercial traffic through the strait is now a fraction of its pre-war level, and America's Central Command says it is ready to resume major combat operations if ordered to.

keys.title: Israel waiting in the wings
keys.text: Israel's security cabinet, chaired by the outgoing prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has reportedly ordered the army to speed up preparations for an attack, according to Israeli media. Mohsen Rezaei warns that every American base “from West Asia to Europe” would become a target.

keys.title: The shadow of the midterms
keys.text: JD Vance wrote that the war explained the Republicans' defeat on 3 November, insisting that the president himself had acknowledged as much. Donald Trump has told him to concentrate on “corruption” in Democratic-run cities and states.

context.t: War breaks out between America, Israel and Iran.

essentials.title: Dogged by suspicions of Chinese espionage, Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia's boss
essentials.standfirst: The co-founder of the AI-chip giant resigned on Thursday, after revelations of an affair with a woman whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing. The chief financial officer, Colette Kress, takes over in the interim.
body: On Thursday 12 November Nvidia announced the resignation “effective immediately” of its chief executive and co-founder, Jensen Huang, 63, who also leaves the board, gave no official reason and named its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim boss, Al Jazeera and The National report.

On 8 November he had admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm, whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing, while Nvidia, which controls about 90% of the market for advanced AI chips, sits at the heart of the Sino-American technology rivalry.

The shares fell by more than 14% at one point on Thursday, the board, now chaired by Harvey Jones, is looking for a successor, and Republican lawmakers are threatening a subpoena to question Mr Huang about the affair's implications for national security.

analysis.title: Chips as a national-security matter
analysis.text: In December 2025 Donald Trump allowed Nvidia's H200 chips, roughly six times as powerful as the H20, to be exported to China, subject to inspections, delivery caps and a 25% levy, Al Jazeera recalls. Chinese firms are said to have ordered more than 2m of them, potentially worth $54bn, though these are orders rather than completed sales. Megaspeed, which reportedly bought $4.8bn-worth of Nvidia chips in two years, has already been investigated in America and Singapore, and the Justice Department has taken over the federal inquiry, according to the New York Times, cited by TechCrunch. The board says it has “no reason” to believe national security was compromised.

keys.title: The White House
keys.text: Donald Trump, who on 8 November still thought Jensen Huang should stay, has suggested Apple's former boss, Tim Cook, as his successor. According to the New York Times, cited by TechCrunch, the president had been told of the suspicions in late 2025.

keys.title: Congress
keys.text: On 5 November three Republican committee chairmen in the House of Representatives asked to question Jensen Huang behind closed doors. Without a reply, a subpoena is likely, John Moolenaar warned on 11 November.

essentials.title: Spain's first general strike since 2012 puts housing at the heart of the election
essentials.standfirst: Hundreds of thousands marched through Spain's big cities on Wednesday, answering the main unions' call to protest against soaring rents and for higher wages. The mobilisation comes less than three weeks before the snap general election of 29 November.
body: On Wednesday 11 November Spain held its first general strike since 2012, called by the CCOO and UGT unions under the banner “wages, housing and prices”, which drew at least 120,000 marchers in Madrid and 55,000 in Barcelona according to the authorities, and many more according to the organisers, Euronews reports.

Rents soared by 87% between 2015 and 2025 while wages rose by about 30%, according to El País, cited by Time, and the average rent swallows almost the entire average salary of 16- to 29-year-olds, according to Spain's Youth Council.

Police made at least 75 arrests, the leader of the People's Party, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, denounced a strike aimed at the opposition, and polls make the right favourite to win the snap election that the prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called for 29 November.

analysis.title: Housing, a generation's fault line
analysis.text: The housing shortfall stands at about 750,000 homes and could exceed 1m by 2028, according to the Bank of Spain, cited by El País, and the share of young people living independently has fallen to 14.5%, a record low, Time reports. Pedro Sánchez called the snap election after parliament threw out two housing decree-laws, opposed by the People's Party, Vox and the Catalan separatists of Junts, according to EUobserver. With the Cortes dissolved, it falls to their Permanent Deputation, where the left and its regional allies have a one-vote majority, to rule on the revised decrees.

keys.title: A contested turnout
keys.text: The unions claim 90% of workers struck in the ports and the car industry, while the CEOE employers' federation puts participation below 5%. Industrial electricity demand fell by 25.6% over the day, according to Euronews.

keys.title: Clashes
keys.text: Police recorded more than a thousand incidents, according to Time. The Madrid branch of CCOO plans to file a complaint after some 20 people were hurt when police charged picket lines.

essentials.title: In South Sudan, Amnesty accuses the UN and Juba of ignoring warnings before a massacre
essentials.standfirst: The rights group says the authorities and UN peacekeepers knew an attack was being prepared on Abiemnom, where at least 213 people were killed on 1 March. The report comes six weeks before the first elections since independence.
body: In a report published this week, Amnesty International says South Sudan's government and the United Nations Mission in South Sudan had enough information and time to prevent the attack of 1 March on Abiemnom, near the Sudanese border, which killed at least 213 people according to the authorities.

According to the group, which interviewed 82 people, between 1,000 and 1,500 gunmen from neighbouring Mayom county shot residents, destroyed more than 230 buildings and looted part of the hospital, while the UN mission reinforced its small garrison only once the assault was over.

The mission blames resources squeezed by budget cuts, Juba did not respond to Amnesty, which wants an independent inquiry, and the country, whose president, Salva Kiir, dissolved the transitional government in September, is due to vote on 22 December for the first time since independence.

analysis.title: Peacekeepers on a shoestring
analysis.text: When the Security Council renewed the UN mission's mandate in April it lowered its troop ceiling from 17,000 to 12,000, the AP notes. At Abiemnom the base was down to 44 soldiers on the eve of the attack, against 74 before, and night patrols had been curtailed, according to evidence gathered by Amnesty. Around a thousand civilians had gathered outside the base on 28 February. The mission's spokeswoman, Priyanka Chowdhury, says it concentrated its resources on protecting the 2,500 or so people sheltering inside its compound, and had repeatedly asked the national army for reinforcements.

keys.title: A town attacked before
keys.text: Abiemnom had already been attacked on 2 April 2025, an assault that killed 52 people according to the UN mission. Amnesty asks why the 40 UN police officers sent after the massacre were not deployed sooner.

keys.title: A tense election
keys.text: South Sudan is due to hold its first elections since independence in 2011 on 22 December. According to UN News, 2.5m people face emergency levels of hunger, and the opposition leader and former vice-president, Riek Machar, remains in detention.

brief.text: An Israeli strike hit the surgical wing of Nasser hospital in Khan Younis on Thursday, killing at least six people according to Gaza's health ministry; Israel's army says it targeted a Hamas commander.

The vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of the former president Joko Widodo, resigned on Thursday after court rulings found his qualifications non-compliant; parliament will choose a successor from two candidates put forward by the president.

Some 136 countries now have multi-hazard early-warning systems, with Africa catching up with the Americas, according to a report by the UN and the World Meteorological Organization presented in Antalya.
